Draft email:

Counsel — Thanks for your letter. We categorically disagree with your characterization of the facts and cannot agree to the unduly narrow discovery parameters you propose; our client requires full production of core project documents and ESI (schedules, change orders, communications, payment records and relevant custodial collections) with substantial completion of document production within 60 days, up to six fact depositions per side, and a contemporaneous plan for expert discovery rather than an automatic stay. We also reserve the right to pursue targeted expedited discovery and to file an early dispositive motion if necessary to protect our record. Please provide your availability this week to meet and confer so we can try to agree on a joint Rule 26(f) report; if we cannot reach agreement we will submit competing proposals to the Court.

rounds.response:
1) Short analysis: concede the five-month fact window and rolling productions as reasonable optics but be firm that a categorical stay of expert discovery is unacceptable because our liability/technical experts are essential to rebut their narrative and to support any early dispositive motion we may bring; we should preserve the right to seek targeted expedited discovery and to file our own early motions if they use sequencing to foreclose necessary fact or expert development. 

2) Proposed discovery plan (for joint Rule 26(f) report): five-month fact discovery period; Rule 26 initial disclosures and rolling ESI/document productions beginning 30 days after disclosures with substantial completion of core project documents (schedules, change orders, custodian communications, payment records) within 60–90 days; up to six fact depositions per side (additional depositions by agreement or leave of court); phased expert discovery—initial disclosures/reports for liability/technical experts 30 days after substantial completion of fact discovery, rebuttal 21 days later, expert depositions to follow within 30 days; damages/economic expert discovery may be held in abeyance pending resolution of liability but parties must exchange expert identities and preliminary reports to avoid unfair surprise; each party reserves the right to seek targeted expedited discovery or to file early dispositive motions, and if we cannot agree on sequencing we will submit competing proposed schedules to the Court. 

3) 26(f) talking points: we support proportionality but oppose a blanket expert stay; explain why liability/technical experts are necessary now and propose the phased expert timeline above; seek agreement on ESI custodians, search terms, rolling production schedule, and a 60–90 day substantial-completion target for core documents; confirm deposition cap and a dispute-resolution pathway (short letter-briefs or an expedited discovery conference with the Court) for any impasses; make clear we will move for relief if they insist on a schedule that improperly curtails fact or expert development. 

4) Two paths to calibrate advocacy: cooperative — accept their five-month window and 30-day rolling production but implement the phased-expert compromise (liability experts proceed, damages deferred); hard-edged — refuse any categorical expert stay, insist on firm expert dates in the joint report, and be prepared to brief the Court and seek expedited discovery and scheduling relief. 

5) If you approve, I’ll send Opposing Counsel the proposed plan before the 26(f) call and use the above talking points; if they remain inflexible we should promptly move to the Court to set a balanced timetable and protect our ability to develop expert proof.
